symptoms: leaf: Angular, yellow spots on older leaves. Spots enlarge and become circular with light brown centers and dark brown borders. In advanced stages, gray centers drop out causing shot-hole or shredded appearance. Under greenhouse conditions, spots may have light centers, rings of olive green tissue, and yellow borders. Severe infection can lead to defoliation. stem_petiole: Elongated spots, helps differentiate from anthracnose, downy mildew, or angular leaf spot. fruit: Darkened, shriveled fruit if infection occurs early at blossom end. roots_flowers: Infections possible but less common.
management: cultural: Use resistant varieties when available Implement good sanitation in fields and greenhouses Remove and destroy infected plant debris Control weed hosts near crops chemical: Preventive fungicide sprays according to label instructions integrated: Combine resistant varieties, sanitation, and fungicide programs to reduce disease incidence
